items.title: Bill Watrous interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 26, 1999
items.q: my band director in high school, Dick Benvenuti, took the time to have music theory class, theory one and two, and harmony one and two. And he taught us an awful lot of things

ctx.x: Yeah, in high school they don’t get much chance to do a small combo, or how many instructors in high school really know how that goes anyway.

Or have the time, Monk. That’s part of the problem. They’re put upon to provide a wind ensemble, a symphonic band, a football field band, and possibly a jazz ensemble. And between all of those things, that’s about all the time they have see? And though, see we were fortunate, my band director in high school, Dick Benvenuti, took the time to have music theory class, theory one and two, and harmony one and two. And he taught us an awful lot of things about harmony and playing a part and blending and listening…
Well let me get back to your entrance into the professional ranks. New York City?
